utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: Our street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: Are our workplace.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: And switch safety to workplace safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We deserve to earn a living without putting our life at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: But we need more than protected bike lane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We also need safe places to park our bike, charge our e-bike batteries, rest, eat, and take a break during long working hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: These are basic needs, not luxuries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: Instead of punishing delivery workers, the city should invest in safe infrastructure and listen to the people who use the street every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We are ready to work with the city, share our experiences, and help develop solutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: I invite, as I said, my leader, Sean Abreu, and all elected officials to spend a day working alongside us as a little worker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: Come ride with us, delivery order, and experience firsthand how difficult and dangerous this work can be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We believe that by working together, we can make our streets safer for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: I urge the City Council to support Intro 0613.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We are not the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We are part of the solution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: We deserve safety, dignity, and respect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Celo Balde
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and for listening to the delivery worker.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next up we have Alejandro from WJP, Los Liberistas.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Antonio Martinez.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Abubakar Key, Muhammad Riaz, Joshua Wood.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Alejandro Grajales, a delivery worker for over 10 years and organizer with the Workers Justice Project, supports Intro 613. He says workers face traffic, dangerous intersections, and disrespect from drivers, and need protected bike lanes, charging, parking, and rest spaces. He invites officials to spend an hour delivering.
chapters.title: Alejandro Grajales supports Intro 613 after 10 years delivering

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Majority Leader Sean Abreu and everyone here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: My name is Alejandro Grajales, and I have been a delivery worker in New York City for over 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: I'm also an organizer with Worker Justice Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: I'm here today to support Intro 0613.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: After more than 10 years making deliveries, I know how dangerous our streets can be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Every day, workers have to deal with traffic, dangerous intersections, and drivers who don't respect us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: That's why we need more protected bike lanes, safe places to charge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: And park our bikes and spaces where workers can take a break.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: We need safer streets, no more tickets or punishment for workers who are just trying to make a living.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: But today, I also want to make any...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: An invitation to all of you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Come and visit our center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Talk to the workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Listen to what they go through every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: And even better, I invite you to spend just one hour, one hour making delivery with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Get on a bike, ride through the city and see what our working conditions are really like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: I believe that one hour on the street can teach you more than many hours sitting in meetings talking about our problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: We are not asking for anything special.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: We are just going to do our jobs and make it home safely for our families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alejandro Grajales
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: You have me for an hour.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Antonio Solis, speaking for Deliveristas Unidos and WJP, supports Intro 0613 in Spanish. He says delivery workers risk their lives and suffer accidents, injuries, lost income, and family hardship, and need protected bike lanes, safe charging, and waiting areas. He also criticizes police fines and harassment.
chapters.title: Antonio Solis, Los Deliveristas Unidos, supports Intro 613 in Spanish

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Buenos días.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Buenos días.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: ¿Cómo está?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Buenos días, el líder es Sona Brown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Un gusto, como siempre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Mi nombre es Antonio Solís.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Represento a los Deliveristas Unidos y a WJP y a miles de trabajadores que hacemos delivery en las aplicaciones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Hoy estoy aquí para apoyar la iniciativa 0613 porque los trabajadores de reparto necesitamos calles más seguras.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Todos los días arriesgamos nuestras vidas para entregar alimentos, medicinas, comida, bebida, alcohol, de todo un poco.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Muchos trabajadores sufren accidentes mientras trabajan, enfrentando lesiones, pérdidas de ingresos y dificultades para mantener a sus familias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Necesitamos más carriles protegidos para bicicletas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: estaciones seguras de carga, para bicicletas eléctricas y espacios designados donde los repartidores podemos esperar pedidos de manera segura.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: También nos preocupa el trato que recibimos por parte de la policía.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Muchos trabajadores se enfrentan a multas, hostigamiento y controles que pueden sentirse desproporcionados mientras...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Intentamos ganarnos la vida.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: En lugar de enfocarse en castigar a los trabajadores, la ciudad debe priorizar la prevención de accidentes mediante infraestructura segura.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Las multas y vigilancia de la policía no sustituyen los carriles protegidos ni resuelven las condiciones peligrosas en las que trabajamos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Pedimos al Consejo Municipal y al Departamento de Transporte que escuchen nuestras voces y nos incluyan en las decisiones que afectan nuestra seguridad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Nuestras calles, es nuestro lugar de trabajo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: No deberíamos arriesgar las vidas para ganarnos la propia vida.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Los trabajadores de reparto no somos el problema.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Somos parte de la solución.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Necesitamos calles más seguras, infraestructura adecuada y respeto por nuestros derechos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Solis
utterances.text: Muchas gracias.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Boubacar Key says delivery drivers deserve safe streets, protected bike lanes, and safe working conditions, not more policing and tickets. He supports Intro 613's 100 miles per year for six years and calls for secure bike parking, charging stations, and rest areas for the over 80,000 delivery workers.
chapters.title: Boubacar Key supports Intro 613 and safer working conditions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Majority Leader Sean Avri, and thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: My name is Abu Akaki, and I have been a daily worker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: I'm here to strongly support Intro 613 because the delivery driver workers deserve safe streets, protected bike lanes, and safe working conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: Not more policing, harassment, and tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: This bill will require the Department of Transportation to build 100 miles of protective bike lanes every year for six years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: This is the kind of investment we need to protect the more than 80,000 daily workers who will keep this city running every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: We appreciate the protected bike lane the city has already built, but our work does not stop there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: We need circular bike parking, safe e-bike sharing station, and designated resting and waiting area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: Instead of spending more money policing delivery workers, the city should invest in protective bike lanes, practical safety solutions, and infrastructure that saves lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: We call on Majority Leader Sean Abre and our elected official to work jointly with Lost Resources in Needles and the Worker Justice Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: To develop policies that protect workers rather than punish them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: And I invite you to do, to experience our daily challenge, see the dangerous street we navigate, the pressure we face, and the risk we take to deliver food to New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: Do not make decisions about our life without understanding our reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Boubacar Key
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and consideration.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Muhammad Riaz, an organizer with the Workers Justice Project, supports Intro 613 and describes a recent accident in Brooklyn on a street with poor lighting and no speed bumps. He calls for protected bike lanes, better lighting, secure bike parking, safe charging, and rest areas.
chapters.title: Muhammad Riaz describes crash and supports protected bike lanes

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Majority Leader Sean Abram.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: My name is Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Mohamed Riyaz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: I am organizer and leader, Worker Justice Project and Los Angeles President.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: I work in New York City almost three years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Today I'm here to support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: intro 0613 which would be required the DOT to install 100 miles of protected bylines every year of six years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Recently I was involved in an accident in Brooklyn on a street which poured lightings and speed bumps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: The darkness made me difficult to see the roads clearly and I was involved in an accident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Our stairs, our workplace.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: We need support, protected bike lanes, better state to lighting, secure bike parkings, safe e-bike charging station, and resting area to the delivery worker can rest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: The city must invest in safer instruction and stand of replying to tickets and enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: I urge city leaders to listen to workers and work with us to create practical solutions that protect lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: We are not problems, we are part of solution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: We deserve safe states, dignity, and a voice in the decision that efforts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: our lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: I invite our majority leader, Shad Abram, to visit our center and work with the delivery workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Then you can know how the delivery workers right in New York City, how they face these problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: So thank you so much for giving me the opportunity to talk.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: In your incident, you said there was poor lighting there too?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Riaz
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Okay, just wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Joshua Wood, a delivery worker with 10 years of experience, supports Intro 613 and says delivery workers are the most efficient way to move goods, reducing car and truck trips. He calls for wider protected bike lanes, daylighting, secure parking, charging, rest areas, and accountability for reckless drivers.
chapters.title: Joshua Wood, delivery worker, supports Intro 613

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Abreu.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: My name is Joshua Wood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: I'm a delivery worker with 10 years of experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: I am here in support of Intro 0613 because we need safer streets through better infrastructure and not more policing and enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Delivery workers are not the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: In my time on the road, I've delivered everything from food to pharmaceuticals to material samples to the outfits being worn at the Met Gala.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: And the reason that all of these goods are delivered

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: by bike, e-bike, and cargo bike is because we are the most efficient way to do it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Every item delivered via micromobility represents one fewer car, one fewer double park truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Residents need us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Businesses need us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: And our streets design needs and our streets design needs to reflect those needs to accommodate the needs of us workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: 100 miles of additional bike lanes doesn't sound unreasonable compared to 80,000 delivery workers on the streets every day, spread across every neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: The approach needs to be comprehensive because our routes are not just limited to the major commuter corridors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: Our road infrastructure was designed knowing that cars, trucks, buses, taxis, they all have different needs, and the same is true for bike infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: We need the major bike lanes to be wide enough to pass to safely pull over without having to ride on the sidewalk when we have to stop at every drop-off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: We also need daylight at intersections, secure bike parking and charging stations, designated rest areas, and a means to address the most reckless drivers who put our lives at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: And again, that's why we're inviting you and DOT officials to meet with delivery workers and ride alongside us to see the challenges that we face firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Wood
utterances.text: The streets are our office, and we are grateful for a seat at the table and making them efficient for everybody.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next up, we have Caitlin Villatoro, Eric Richardson.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Sandra Huambachano, Kate Cole, and David Bartner.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And can we get an extra chair, sergeants?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Should we need it for the child?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Nice.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Caitlin Villatoro, New York City Policy Fellow at the New York League of Conservation Voters, says safe streets must be the standard and supports Vision Zero Reimagined. She supports Intro 1070, Intro 1153, and urges consideration of Intro 511 for universal daylighting at a minimum of 100 intersections per year.
chapters.title: Caitlin Villatoro, NYLCV, supports Vision Zero Reimagined and Intro 1070

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Caitlin Vietoro, and I'm the New York City Policy Fellow at the New York League of Conservation Voters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Abreu and members of the Transportation Committee for this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We'll be submitting longer written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: As outlined by Vision Zero's core principles, not one single traffic fatality is acceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Safe streets must be the standard for any city, and all forms of travel, walking, biking, or public transit should be enjoyed without fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Since its implementation in 2014, we've seen Vision Zero launch life-saving measures that encourage pedestrian safety and design streets for better travel alternatives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We've long advocated that these safety measures and sustainability go hand in hand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We applaud the Mamdani.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: administration for their demonstrated commitment to Vision Zero with the release of Vision Zero Reimagined.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Overall, we need comprehensive solutions to eliminate traffic deaths and injuries, and the eight goals outlined set a clear path to achieving this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: The need for funding and implementing Vision Zero policies are even more urgent given recent traffic fatalities and injuries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: The city must implement SAMI's law and continue investing in safe bike and e-bike infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We support the passage of Intro 1070, a two-year low-traffic neighborhood pilot program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: LTNs limit the amount of cars that cut through neighborhoods, making streets safer, quieter, and more welcoming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: It represents what New Yorkers want for their communities, fewer cars speeding through their blocks and more livable streets where people come first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We also support Intro 1153, which will curb speeding by requiring the worst speeding offenders to install a device that would force them to go at the speed limit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: And we would like to urge the City Council to consider Intro 511 as part of the Vision Zero Toolkit, implementing daylighting barriers at a minimum of 100 intersections per year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Daylighting makes pedestrians at crosswalks more visible to drivers and can reduce the chance of collisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We are moving in the right direction with street and pedestrian safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: This reimagined strategy for Vision Zero is what the city needs, but cannot be executed without proper funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We look forward to working with the council.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Eric Richardson, former Deputy Chief Fleet Officer for New York City, testifies that intelligent speed assistance works on low-end and high-end vehicles and all sizes from the city pilot. He urges implementation by May 2027 and says the current Intro 1153 is too broad and exempts too many vehicles, suggesting city fleet and regulated fleet requirements.
chapters.title: Eric Richardson testifies on intelligent speed assistance implementation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: My name is Eric Richardson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: I'm the former Deputy Chief Fleet Officer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: For the city of New York, and I now advise governments and commercial fleets on vehicle safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: I was actually part of the team who put the first 50-vehicle pilot in place for New York City vehicles and actually had the pleasure to speak on a panel with now Mayor Madami about intelligence speed assist back in 2023.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: I want to thank you for getting this legislation finally on paper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: New York State was one of the first states to introduce the law, but not one of the first to pass the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: In fact, there are many states who are now implementing the law that they've already passed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: I do think that one of the things we need to do is make sure we're doing all the work, taking all the action, and dedicating everything we can to make sure that this law is in place and implemented no later than the scheduled date of May 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: As is, we're going to have to wait for violations to be issued, time for notifications to be made, installation time, and quite frankly, I don't think anybody in this room wants to explain to a family that lose a loved one when we have the power to stop the tragedy from happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: I want to emphasize that ISA works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: We know it works on low-end vehicles, Fords, Chevys, Toyotas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: We know it works on high-end vehicles, Porsches, Mercedes, and we know from the city pilot that it works on all sizes of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: The reason why I say this is because sometimes laws and good intentions need to catch up to technology.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: That is not the case here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: Also, I want to emphasize that I do understand that there's a difference between regular vehicles, commercial vehicles, and city vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: But quite frankly, I think the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: current introduction is too broad, exempts too many vehicles, the City Council can pass a law similar to truck side guards that covers city vehicles, regulated fleets, trade waste to ensure that these vehicles are just as safe as everyone else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: The legislation as introduced is a strong step towards saving lives on our roads, and I look forward to working with the council, the sponsors, and your staff to move this towards a vote, get it to the mayor's desk for signature, and implementing it without delay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Richardson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Kate Coley, a resident who walks the city, describes Atlantic and Flatbush as a horrible intersection for women, children, and disabled pedestrians. She says right turns back up school buses and block crosswalks, and urges action at the intersection.
chapters.title: Kate Coley testifies on dangerous Atlantic and Flatbush intersection

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: Hi, this is Kate Coley, and thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: I am a resident, and I walk the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: And one of the big intersections that I have found that is just horrible for women and children

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: handicapped is Atlantic and Flatbush.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: And I don't see any mitigating devices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: I see people turning right out of desperation because, you know, it's like one

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: car turns right on that intersection per light.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: So you'll have this backup of school buses, and they'll cut off people in the crosswalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: So this is a hot area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: Watch it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: I am just, something needs to be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: This particular intersection, this particular time, when I interview UPS drivers or anyone, they say this is one of the worst intersections in the world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: In the whole city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kate Coley
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I mean, the city ought to be looking at that and doing something about it.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Sandra Wambachano, founder of We Strive for a Place to Ride, testifies about e-bike regulation and consumer product classification. She says low-speed e-bikes lack automotive VINs and insurance, warns registration mandates harm bike shops and riders, and calls for infrastructure accountability rather than blaming grieving parents.
chapters.title: Sandra Wambachano testifies on e-bike regulation and consumer product classification

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: My name is Sandra.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I am a neighbor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I'm originally from New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: This is my second home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I do have a lot of ride outs, so I'm sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Once again, my name is Sandra Wambachano.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I am founder of We Strive for a Place to Ride.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I am representing thousands of recreational transport riders, delivery couriers, and working class families who face intense regulatory bottlenecks across our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: First, standard low-speed and recreational vehicles are classified explicitly as consumer products under Title 15 United States Code, Section 2085,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: overseen by Consumer Product Safety Commission, which is a 15 U.S.C.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Code, Subsection 2085-Low, because they are manufactured under

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: bicycle and product safety standards rather than automotive frameworks, these frames do not possess a 17-digit National Highway Traffic Safety Administration VIN.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: When municipal codes seek to enforce motor vehicle level tracking or local registration matrices on these consumer frames, it triggers an unworkable paradox.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Major insurance companies do not issue standard automotive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: liability policies to consumer items lacking an automotive VIN.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Forcing our workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: When a neighboring state implemented sweeping registration laws this past July, the severe economic damage to local bike shops forced lawmakers to frantically introduce Senate Bill

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: This month to reverse the mandates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Most tragically, the lack of proactive education is costing lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Children have died on public roads, and instead of taking accountability of lack infrastructure, the system is hitting grieving parents with child neglect.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: I will submit the documentation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Wambachano
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We'll make sure to read it.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Please do give us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I hope we can partner up in many things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I appreciate you coming in today.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: David Bartner, a Brooklyn father of three, says dangerous driving happens daily near his home and a car with about 20 speeding tickets and Jersey plates nearly hit him. He says the danger is huge vehicles, not delivery bikes, and wants children to be able to bike independently.
chapters.title: David Bartner testifies as parent about dangerous streets

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Hey, my name's David Bartner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: I'm a father.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: I live in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: I have three kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't know why I'm emotional, but every day someone does something dangerous in a car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Every day near our house.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And there's no accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: The other day I was almost hit by a car that had like 20 speeding tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And I had jersey plates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And that car's been looked up on How's My Driving like 10 times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: It's absurd.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: This guy knows how to cross the street, but he can't because it's so dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And that's why all parents don't let their five and six-year-olds cross the street on their own.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: That is no kind of a society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: We have to be moving fast to allow our children to grow independently where the consequences of a mistake are not life and death.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: The danger is not delivery bikes, who have gotten a lot better, I would say, in the last couple of years on the streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: The danger are these huge vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Who are making noise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Everything as small as making noise to wake these kids up from naps, to disturb our peaceful neighborhoods, to slaughtering our children for something as simple as riding a bike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: I really want to ask the city is when he's 10 years old, he's six.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: When he's 10, will he be able to ride a bike to his friend's house on his own?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I think probably not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: But that's a simple goal, and we should aspire to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And anyone who's trying to get in our way is getting in our way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: in the way of very simple progress that is attainable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: We see it in other cities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: We see it in other places.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: The reason parents don't let their kids do this stuff anymore is because in the 70s, in the 60s, look up the numbers of kids who died by cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: It was horrible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: So parents started keeping their kids indoors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And go back in New York City history, you'll see protests from children, from mothers in the 40s and 50s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: They gave up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: And a lot of them left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Bartner
utterances.text: Let's build streets for our workers, for our children, for joy and for beauty.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you for your heartfelt testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Government needs to do a lot, a lot more.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: But appreciate you taking your time and bringing your kids with you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We're doing it for them.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Fakrul Hassan, Modi So, Jairi Castro, John Stephen, Bubakar Barry.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: As a reminder to please state your name before you speak.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Yairi Castro supports Intro 0613 and says newly built streets should be reviewed with the workers who use them. She asks that delivery workers' experience be part of monitoring, not just initial conversations, to improve future projects.
chapters.title: Yairi Castro supports Intro 613 and post-implementation review with workers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Buen día, agradezco la oportunidad de hablar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Mi nombre es Yairi y pido al consejo que escuche a quienes usamos estas calles para trabajar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Una calle recién construida debe revisarse con las personas que la utilizan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Después de abrir un carril, los trabajadores pueden decir si la ruta conecta bien, si una señal se entiende y si el acceso a los puntos de entrega funciona.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Esa evaluación permite aprender y mejorar los siguientes proyectos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Apoyamos la inversión de INT 0613-2026 y pedimos que la experiencia de los repartidores forme parte del seguimiento, no solo de la conversación inicial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Apoyo al INT 0613-2026 y la invitación a trabajar directamente con nuestra organización.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Planifiquemos estas mejoras juntos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yairi Castro
utterances.text: Muchas gracias.

chapters.summary: John Carrero says street safety is also a labor issue and delivery workers should not have to lose a day's pay or travel far to participate in meetings. He asks for flexible schedules, accessible information in community languages, and DOT consultation with workers during Intro 613 implementation.
chapters.title: John Carrero says street safety is a labor issue

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Buenos días, mi nombre es John Carrero y trabajo en entregas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: La seguridad de las calles es también un asunto laboral.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Los repartidores no deberíamos tener que perder un día de trabajo para participar en reuniones públicas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Pedimos horarios flexibles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Opciones accesibles e información en los idiomas de nuestras comunidades para que todos podamos compartir nuestra experiencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: WGP y Deliveries Unidos pueden ayudar a conectar a los trabajadores del Departamento de Transporte con las siglas DOT para que nuestras voces sean escuchadas durante la implementación del

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Apoyo esta iniciativa y pido al DOT consulte a los repartidores.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Somos parte de nuestra solución y merecemos calles seguras para trabajar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Carrero
utterances.text: Muchas gracias.

chapters.summary: Bubakar Barry, a delivery worker for three years, testifies about unfair account deactivations. He says workers are deactivated without being told what rule they violated, that he was deactivated twice, and that Uber and other apps do not ask for the worker's side. He calls on the Council to address job losses.
chapters.title: Bubakar Barry testifies on unfair delivery account deactivations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Thanks so much for giving me time, opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Hello, I'm Bubakar Bari.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: I have been a delivery worker here in New York for three years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: I want to share my experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Delivery workers are frequently having their account deactivated without even knowing what they supposedly did wrong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: I have personally had my account deactivated twice, both times without being told what rule I allegedly violated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Sometimes, when we arrive to make a delivery, we encounter an intoxicated customer who later files a false report against the delivery worker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Uber and other apps don't even bother to ask the worker for their side of the story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: We simply proceed to deactivate the account.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: We are calling of the city council to look into the issue as people are losing their job every single day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: I am currently out of work because my account was deactivated, which I devastated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: given the high daily and monthly living expenses here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: For instance, for example, Grohop deactivated my account.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: I spoke with one of their representatives who admitted that the deactivation was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bubakar Barry
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Christopher Leon Johnson supports every bill on the agenda, including Intro 613, and urges Abreu to spend a week as a deliverista without security detail. He also says the city needs to phase out unsafe e-bikes and protect workers from unfair deactivation.
chapters.title: Christopher Leon Johnson supports bills and invites officials to deliver

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Yeah, hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: My name is Christopher Leon Johnson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I support every bill on the ticker, including Intro 613.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I want to say this right now that I know that a lot of these guys here, including the top people like Ligia and Alejandro, are telling you that you should take at least an hour to be a Delarista for a day, Mr.

utterances.text: Abreu.

utterances.text: Just be you.

utterances.text: Be with them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: And you understand what's going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: You could do the same thing and post yourself all over social media with Be The Liberista.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Wear the same stuff they're wearing and you'll see what them guys go through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I think you have a bigger outlight about their fights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Being a libertarian.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I want to say this right now about the bill, 613, that, yeah, we need protected bike lanes, but at the same time, we need to find a way to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: do the phase out for these e-bikes that we see outside the Arista hub with the batteries that look like time bombs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: That'd be my advice going forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: They need to have like a real program to get those bikes out of the way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: It doesn't matter if you have protected bike lanes to the top, like Brooklyn Bridge or like some of the most dangerous areas in the city where you have to have the protected bike lanes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: But if there's no real bike structure, like the physical bike these guys use to be taken out and get replaced with like Joko bikes or like Wiz bikes or real regulated bikes, it does nothing for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Going forward, the city council need to get back to the drawing board to where it's at.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: They need to find a way to make sure these guys and gals don't get unfairly deactivated more because even they're on the bike lane and they need to be helped instead of penalized for trying to do their job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: So I know it's kind of short, but I support the bills and the ticker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: And like I said, do a week as a delivery store.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: For the record, I don't have security detail.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: También tengo otra sugerencia de que...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: No entiendo ni comprendo el por qué las personas de los restaurantes nos tratan a nosotros tan mal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Deberían de tener el mismo trato hacia nosotros porque somos las personas que recibimos clientes, las órdenes a los clientes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Igual como los clientes se encuentran dentro de la tienda, reciben el trato.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Diferente que no nos lo dan a nosotros.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Muchas gracias.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Gracias por sus testimonios.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Es correcto que por ese solo error te activaron de la compañía, de Uber.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: En realidad...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Injusto.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: En realidad, en realidad, también me sucedió porque un momento de frío olvidé mis guantes y

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: cuando quise activar la cuenta que le di para entregar, para recibirla, la recibí.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Pero el dedo se me quedó pegado como en la pantalla y le di también a la broma para entregada y llamo al soporte de Uber y le digo que el por qué ellos no me podían proporcionar el...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: la dirección de la persona porque yo tenía ya el pedido y yo lo había hecho y ya no lo podía cancelar.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Injusto.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Gracias por su testimonio.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Ok, muchas gracias.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Pase buena.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Buen día.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio César Frías
utterances.text: Ya nos podemos retirar.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Sí, pardon.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yeah, this panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Está retirado.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Anyone else here would like to testify in person?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And if you would like to testify in person, please fill out an appearance card.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Seeing none, we'll transition to Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And on Zoom, we'll begin first with Kathleen Collins, followed by Tal Litwin.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Kathleen Collins, a native New Yorker with a disability, testifies that Vision Zero must ensure wheelchair-accessible ride-hail vehicles and proper securement. She says she rarely gets a proper seatbelt, shoulder belt, and four-point wheelchair securement, and fears retaliation if she complains.
chapters.title: Kathleen Collins testifies on accessibility and wheelchair securement in ride-hail

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for doing this all day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: We really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: My name is Kathleen Collins.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I'm a native New Yorker with a disability from birth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: And I'd like to just mention a few things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: First, if Vision Zero Reimagined expects people with disabilities to rely on such things as Uber, Lyft, and taxis, the New York City must ensure that enough wheelchair-accessible vehicles are available and that those vehicles provide safe,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: properly secured rides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: As a wheelchair user, I cannot take for granted that I will be able to get into a vehicle, travel safely, and arrive at my destination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Every time I use the taxi or ride share service, I face questions that other passengers may never have to consider.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Will the vehicle accommodate my wheelchair?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Will I be properly secured with a seatbelt, shoulder belt, and four-point securement?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Will the driver even pick me up after accepting my ride?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I have an experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I have experienced receiving a proper seatbelt, shoulder belt, and four-point wheelchair securement so rarely that it is like spotting a unicorn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Despite instructions and pictures posted inside the vehicle showing how wheelchairs must be secured and that there needs to be a seatbelt and shoulder belt, these basic safety requirements are still not...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Consistently met.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: In fact, I hardly ever get a proper seatbelt or shoulder belt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Are disabled passengers expected to prosecute every violator only to risk being denied future rides?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I mean, I could spend my whole life bringing in complaints, but I don't want to do that to their drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I like them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: They help me, but they need to be...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I don't know what's, there's a disconnect that needs to be fixed so that they understand that we need our seatbelts and shoulder belts and a wheelchair seatbelt or shoulder belt is not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Just one other thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Vi refuses, must also be...

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Next up, we have Tal Litwin, followed by Felipe Castillo.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Al, you're unmuted.

chapters.summary: The committee calls Tal Litwin for remote testimony, but staff reports no response. Abreu moves to Felipe Castillo.
chapters.title: Committee calls Tal Litwin, receives no response, moves to Felipe Castillo

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Paul's not responding.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right, Felipe Castillo.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I believe that's my constituent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Felipe Castillo, a Harlem resident and Community Board 9 member, says road violence is preventable and urges the Council to implement evidence-based measures. He supports universal hardened daylighting, Sammy's Law across Manhattan, Stop Super Speeders, low-traffic neighborhoods, and redesigning streets for vulnerable users, and voices support for delivery workers.
chapters.title: Felipe Castillo urges evidence-based street safety measures

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Hello, can you hear me all right?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We sure can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: All right, great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Thanks so much, Majority Leader Avereo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Like you said, I am one of your constituents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Thanks for having this panel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: I hope you've been brushing up on your French.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Merci beaucoup is all I know, my friend.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Okay, sounds good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: So my name is Felipe Castillo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: I am a resident of Harlem and I'm active in Community Board 9 in Manhattan, among other organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: I'm not speaking for them today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: I am going to say that road violence is preventable and I urge...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: The city council to implement the evidence-based measures that have been discussed today to decrease morbidity and mortality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Among them, I would say installing universal hardened daylighting, implementing Stammy's law, especially on the entirety of the island of Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Nine out of 12 community boards have requested that the speed limit be lowered to 20 miles an hour.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: So might as well go for all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Of the island of Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Implement the Stop Super Speeders program that has evidence behind it, and installing low traffic neighborhoods, redesign the roadways with priority for the most vulnerable users,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: not for the storage of a private vehicle on a public roadway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: And these measures are all measures that have the potential for a high impact effect at a low cost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: And lastly, I want to support all the distributors, especially those who attended today and are fighting for the protected and exclusive bicycles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Muchas gracias a ellos y a ellas y continúen en esa lucha.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: Que los apoyamos.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Gracias, Felipe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felipe Castillo
utterances.text: De nada.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Going back to Tal Litwin, are you on Zoom?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Tal, you're unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: Abreu asks if any registered testifiers remain who have not been called; none respond. He thanks the administration and public, closes the hearing, and adjourns.
chapters.title: Chair Abreu closes public testimony and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If we inadvertently missed anyone who registered to testify today and has yet to be called, please use the Zoom raise hand function if you are testifying remotely, and you will be called in the order your hand has been raised.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: If you are testifying in person, please come to the dais.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Going once, going twice.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Seeing none.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will now close the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you to the members of the administration and members of the public who have joined us today.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This hearing is adjourned.

summary: The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure held an oversight hearing on Vision Zero and several street safety bills, including Intro 46, Intro 113, Intro 613, Intro 1070, Intro 1153, and Res 687.

DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn, NYPD officials, BIC, and public advocates testified on traffic fatalities, enforcement trends, daylighting, protected bike lanes, low-traffic neighborhoods, intelligent speed assistance, side guards, and implementation timelines.

The hearing featured extensive public testimony from families of crash victims, delivery workers, accessibility advocates, and safe-streets organizations, with repeated calls for faster implementation and stronger street safety infrastructure.
title: Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure
topic: Oversight - Vision Zero: Evaluating NYC's Street Safety Strategy
